def: AWS's service for logs, metrics and alarms. Where you watch what your system is doing.
A set of log streams that belong together, such as every server's logs for one app. Retention is set here.
The log lines from one source, such as one server, in time order, inside a log group.
How long CloudWatch keeps log events before deleting them. Defaults to never expire, so always set it.
Writing each log line as JSON with named fields, so logs can be filtered, counted and averaged instead of just read.
A program installed on a server that ships its log files, and metrics like memory and disk use, to CloudWatch.
A rule on a log group that turns matching log lines into a metric, such as a count of ERROR lines. Only counts lines that arrive after it exists.
CloudWatch's query tool for logs: filter, count and group log lines with commands joined by |.
The value that 95% of measurements are below. For response times it shows the slow minority that an average hides.
A rule that watches one metric against a threshold and changes state — OK, ALARM or INSUFFICIENT_DATA — sending a notification when it fires.
The "M out of N" setting: how many of the last N periods must cross the threshold before an alarm fires.
An alarm switching back and forth between OK and ALARM, usually because the threshold sits on the metric's normal level.
What an alarm assumes when a period has no data: missing, good, bad, or keep the current state.
A named channel in Simple Notification Service. Alarms publish to it; its subscriptions deliver the message by email, text or to other systems.
An alarm that combines other alarms with a rule, such as A AND B, so one incident sends one notification.
What happens when alarms fire without needing action: people learn to ignore them, including the real ones.
AWS's record of every API call in your account: who made it, what it was, when, from where, and whether it worked.
The free, always-on view of the last 90 days of management events in one region.
A CloudTrail event for creating, changing, deleting or describing a resource. Recorded in event history by default.
A CloudTrail event for reading or writing inside a resource, such as an S3 file. Only recorded by a trail that has them turned on.
A CloudTrail setting that copies events to files in an S3 bucket, so you keep them as long as you like, from every region.
A firewall for a whole subnet. Unlike a security group it can deny, and it doesn't remember connections, so replies need their own rule.
A server's boot output, fetched by AWS without any network access to the server. The place to look when an instance won't boot.
A written, tested procedure for one situation, exact enough that anyone on call could follow it at 3am.
Following a runbook for real, with a stopwatch, to find gaps before an incident does.
A short written account of an incident — what happened, why, and what will change — shared so everyone learns.
Investigating incidents by asking what made a mistake possible, not who made it, so people can say what really happened.
